items.text: Classifying topoi
A small category $C$ with finite inverse limits $\;=\;$ an algebraic structure $T_C$ definable by finite inverse limits.
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{lex}}(C,E)\;=\;T_C(E)\quad\text{(realizations of the structure in } E)
For topoi $E$: a structure of this type in $E$ = a morphism of topoi $E\to\widehat C$.
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{top}}(E,\widehat C)\;\simeq\;T_C(E)
$\widehat C$ is the classifying topos of $T_C$ (on topoi).
Examples
Groups. $C^{\circ}$ = groups of finite presentation.
\widehat C=\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\{\text{groups of finite presentation}\},\mathbf{Sets}\bigr)\quad\text{(covariant functors)}
Commutative rings. Rings of finite presentation over $\mathbb Z$; covariant functors to Sets.
Opposite category: affine schemes of finite type over $\mathbb Z$; the classifying topos is its presheaf category.
Schemes: particular such functors, ring $\mapsto$ set.
Problem 1 : enveloping topos of a small category
For a variable topos $E$, interpret functors $C\to E$ as morphisms of topoi (left exact among others).
First adjoin finite inverse limits: $C\subset\widetilde C$ full subcategory.
\widetilde C\subset \operatorname{Hom}(C,\mathbf{Sets})^{\circ}\ \text{generated by } C \text{ under finite inverse limits}
Two steps: finite products, then kernels; no transfinite construction. These are the objects of finite presentation.
Universal property of $\widetilde C$:
\operatorname{Hom}(C,E)\;\simeq\;\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{lex}}(\widetilde C,E)
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{lex}}(\widetilde C,E)\;\simeq\;\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{top}}\bigl(E,\widehat{\widetilde C}\bigr)
Enveloping topos in two steps: add finite inverse limits, then take the hat.
$\operatorname{Hom}(C,-)$ is itself an elementary algebraic structure; problem 1 is understood.
Problem 2 : inverting arrows
A topos $E$ and a family $\Sigma$ of arrows of $E$.
$\Delta$-functors $E\to F$: commute with arbitrary direct limits and finite inverse limits.
Wanted: a universal $E[\Sigma^{-1}]$ with
\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}\bigl(E[\Sigma^{-1}],F\bigr)\;\simeq\;\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta,\Sigma}(E,F)
($\Sigma$ need not be small.) Index $\Sigma$: only functors sending $\Sigma$ to isomorphisms.
Saturate $\Sigma$ under finite inverse limits and direct limits: the problem does not change; calculus of fractions.
Saturated families of arrows $\;\leftrightarrow\;$ subtopoi of $E$ (SGA exercise): stable under base change, and belonging to $\Sigma$ is local.
Subtopoi
$i\colon E'\to E$ is an embedding if $i_*$ is fully faithful,
equivalently $i^*$ is a localisation (category of fractions of $E$ by the arrows $i^*$ inverts).
Subtopoi $=$ strictly full subcategories of $E$ that are topoi, with a left exact left adjoint to the inclusion.
On a category $C$: topologies on $C$ $\leftrightarrow$ such subcategories of $\widehat C$ (sheaves).
X\to Y \text{ continuous: } \operatorname{Top}(X)\to\operatorname{Top}(Y)\text{ embedding}\iff \mathcal T_X=f^{-1}\mathcal T_Y
Sober spaces: $f$ injective, topology induced. Subspaces are particular subtopoi; there are more.
Factorisation: $F\to E$ factors through $E'$ iff $f_*$ lands in $E'$, iff $f^*$ factors through the quotient $E\to E'$.
Bijection: subtopoi of $E$ $\leftrightarrow$ saturated families of arrows.
X\in E'\iff \operatorname{Hom}(Z,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Y,X)\text{ bijective for all } (u\colon Y\to Z)\in\Sigma
So $E[\Sigma^{-1}]$ is a topos: problem 2 is solved by a subtopos; every subtopos arises this way.
If $E=\widetilde C$ is sheaves for a topology on $C$: subtopoi $\leftrightarrow$ finer topologies on $C$ (more covering families).
Subtheories of a theory represented by $E$ $\leftrightarrow$ topologies finer than the given one.
Theorem (algebraic theories)
The algebraic theories (of the kind $\Delta$ considered) are exactly those represented by topoi.
$E$ a topos, $B\colon I\to E$ with $I$ a discrete category ($I$ = set of base objects):
B \text{ is basic}\iff B(I)\text{ is generating in } E
Easy half: by problems 1 and 2, built step by step, theories are representable (generators kept).
Converse: if $I\to E$ is generating, $E$ presents an algebraic theory on the base objects $I$. Three steps, no transfinite construction.
$T_0$: the empty structure on $I$.
$T_1$: add the arrows of $E$ between objects of $I$ and their composites; $I_1$ the full subcategory generated by $I$.
T_1(E)=\operatorname{Hom}(I_1,E)\quad\text{(on all categories)}
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{top}}(E,F)\subset\operatorname{Hom}(I_1,F)$: the continuous ones.
$I_1$ generating: $E$ is a subtopos of $\widehat{I_1}$, i.e. $E=\widetilde{I_1}$ for the induced topology.
Subtopos = invert certain arrows of $\widehat{I_1}$.
Missing: that $\widehat{I_1}$ represents an algebraic structure on the base set $I$.

Correction of SGA : strict generators
$C\subset E$ full subcategory. Conditions:
\text{(a)}\quad E\to\widehat E\to\widehat C\ \text{ fully faithful}
\text{(b)}\quad \forall X\in E:\ X=\varinjlim_{Y\in C/X}Y
\text{(c)}\quad \forall X\ \exists (Y_i\to X),\ Y_i\in C,\ \text{strictly epimorphic}
(b) $\Rightarrow$ (c) holds; the converse is false.
Counterexample
$E$ = groups, $C=\{\mathbb Z\}$ (full subcategory); $\mathbb Z*\mathbb Z$ is the sum of two copies of $\mathbb Z$, so (c) holds,
but $\mathbb Z*\mathbb Z$ is not the limit of the system over $C/X$: $\widehat C$ = sets with an action of the monoid $G=(\mathbb Z,\times)$.
The two inclusions $\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z*\mathbb Z$ form a strictly epimorphic family; all maps $\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z*\mathbb Z$ do not.
Adding morphisms can destroy strict epimorphy.
Source of the error: products distributive over sums were taken for granted.
False in general: $(X_i\to X)$ strictly epimorphic $\iff \coprod X_i\to X$ strictly epimorphic.
True if products exist and are distributive over arbitrary sums.
Statement meant: "all epimorphic families are strictly epimorphic", not "all epimorphisms are".
\text{(c}')\quad \forall X\ \exists (Y_i\to X),\ Y_i\in C,\ \text{strictly and universally epimorphic}
Then (b) holds. Proof (idea): the family of all $Y\to X$ over $C/X$ is again strictly (and universally) epimorphic.
\text{(b}')\quad (Y\to X)_{Y\in C/X}\ \text{strictly epimorphic}\ ;\qquad \text{(c}')\Rightarrow\text{(b}')\Rightarrow\text{(b)}
(b$'$) $\Rightarrow$ (b): for any $Z$ look at the functor $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(T,Z)$ …
